hints: Look closely at the level of detail in this micrograph, especially the tiny black dots on the folded membranes and the sharp double membranes. What does that level of resolution tell you?

Recall the resolution limits: a light microscope resolves down to about 200 nm, while an electron microscope resolves down to about 0.1 nm. Which named structure in this cell is about 20 nm in diameter and so can only be resolved by one of these?
walkthrough:
**Observe what is actually resolved**

Look at the image. You can see extensive folded rough endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria with membranes, part of the nucleus, and tiny dark dots which are ribosomes.

The image is black and white, very sharp, and shows ultrastructure in fine detail.

**Apply the resolution rule**

The key idea is resolution, not just magnification. A light microscope cannot resolve objects smaller than about $200 \text{ nm}$.

$$ \text{light resolution} \approx 200 \text{ nm}, \quad \text{electron resolution} \approx 0.1 \text{ nm} $$

Ribosomes are only about $20 \text{ nm}$ in diameter, so they are far too small to be seen with a light microscope.

**Conclude the microscope type**

Because ribosomes and fine membrane details are clearly resolved here, this must be a transmission electron micrograph.

Larger structures like the nucleus or chloroplasts can be seen with both types, so they cannot prove which microscope was used.

options.A: The nucleus is large enough to be seen with both a light microscope and an electron microscope, so its presence does not prove an electron microscope was used.
options.B: The endoplasmic reticulum is clearly visible as the stacked membranes filling most of the cell, so the first part of the statement is incorrect.
options.C: The small oval organelles are mitochondria, not chloroplasts, and chloroplasts can be seen with a light microscope anyway, so this does not identify the microscope.
options.D: Ribosomes are about 20 nm in size and can only be resolved by an electron microscope, so seeing them proves an electron microscope was used.
